solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Intimidate son interrupting discussion in plant

parts.note: to cow someone is to intimidate them

indicators.note: the son's letter breaks into the discussion, sitting inside it

parts.note: a parley is a discussion, especially between enemies

explanation.surface: A bully keeps cutting into a talk about a garden plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Cow parsley is a common white-flowered umbellifer of British hedgerows and verges.

clue.text: Surpass old-fashioned tourists finally on excursion

parts.note: out means out of fashion

indicators.note: only the final letter of tourists is used

parts.note: a trip is an excursion

explanation.surface: Old-style sightseers end up on an outing.
explanation.definitionFit: To outstrip is to go faster or further than, which is to surpass.

clue.text: This standard giving rise to censure

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: a rap is a rebuke or censure, as a rap on the knuckles

explanation.surface: Some standard practice leads to criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Par is the accepted normal level, as in 'up to par', a standard.

clue.text: River horse, or cow, by the sound of it

indicators.note: it is the spoken form that matters, so a word pronounced the same is wanted

parts.note: roan is a mixed coat colour seen in both horses and cattle, and a roan is such an animal

explanation.surface: A riddle about a river creature that is part horse, part cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhône is a major European river flowing from Switzerland through France to the Mediterranean.

clue.text: More recent article identifies site of Roman basilica

parts.note: later means more recent
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A newer piece of writing pinpoints where a Roman church stood.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lateran in Rome is home to St John Lateran, the cathedral basilica of the Pope as bishop.

clue.text: Singing and shouting odds regularly inside

indicators.note: the picked letters are placed inside the shouting word

parts.note: yelling is shouting

indicators.note: taking letters at a regular interval, the first and third of odds

explanation.surface: Someone sings and yells about betting odds.
explanation.definitionFit: Yodelling is a style of singing with rapid switches between chest voice and falsetto.

clue.text: Person singing in new boat

parts.note: an ark is a boat, as Noah's

explanation.surface: Someone sings aboard a newly built vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Singing' is slang for informing to the police, not making music.
explanation.definitionFit: A nark is a police informer, someone who 'sings' by giving information to the authorities.

clue.text: Accepting new power, not a single craftsman is unbiased

indicators.note: the outer phrase accepts the other letters, taking them in

parts.note: no means not a single, as in 'no craftsman'
an artisan is a craftsman
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: No craftsman will accept new power, so all remain impartial.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-partisan means not supporting any party or faction, hence impartial.

clue.text: Cut out part of support covering financial centre

indicators.note: the support covers the other letters, which go inside it

parts.note: a rest is a support, as the cue rest in snooker
EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial centre

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes part of a support covering a City office.
explanation.definitionFit: To resect is the surgical term for removing part of an organ or bone.

clue.text: Furore over books in part of Belfast

parts.note: a storm is an outburst or furore
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: An uproar about books breaks out somewhere in Belfast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' looks like a link meaning 'about' but supplies the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Stormont is the district of east Belfast that houses Northern Ireland's parliament buildings.

clue.text: Scandinavian food tucked into by a knight on board

indicators.note: the food has the other letters placed inside it, as food is tucked into by a diner

parts.note: a dish is an item of food
in chess notation the knight is N

explanation.surface: A knight on a ship tucks into some Scandinavian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Danish describes someone or something from Denmark, a Scandinavian country.

clue.text: Extremely significant widespread conflict

indicators.note: only the extreme letters, first and last, of the following word are taken

parts.note: rife means widespread, prevalent

explanation.surface: A war correspondent's phrase for a big, far-reaching conflict.
explanation.definitionFit: Strife is bitter disagreement or fighting, a synonym of conflict.

clue.text: Unusually tiny, listens with determination

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual way, so the letters are put in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Someone small listens in a strange manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistently means persistently, refusing to yield, which shows determination.

clue.text: Administered church, inspiring priest's trust

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so the outer letters take the priest inside

parts.note: to run something is to administer it; ran is the past tense
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel; the 's is part of the surface
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A church run by a priest whom the congregation trusts.
explanation.definitionFit: Reliance is dependence or confidence placed in someone, a synonym of trust.

clue.text: Student of life misused Bitcoins site

indicators.note: a misused thing is put to wrong use, so these letters are wrongly arranged and need reworking

explanation.surface: Someone has abused a website trading in cryptocurrency.
explanation.definitionFit: A bioscientist studies the life sciences, biology in its broad sense.

clue.text: Off-the-cuff claim to be on time at university

parts.note: saying 'I'm' claims to be something
prompt means on time

explanation.surface: A student insists they arrive punctually at college, speaking without notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu means done without preparation, the same as an unrehearsed off-the-cuff remark.

clue.text: Lock up woman concerned with protecting elected member

indicators.note: the woman surrounds and shields the member

parts.note: Iris is a woman's name
an MP is an elected Member of Parliament
on means about, concerned with

explanation.surface: A woman is looking after her local MP.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprison someone is to lock them up in jail.

clue.text: A game is set up, oddly, for a day in church

indicators.note: oddly means in a strange way, so these letters are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: A game has been arranged in a peculiar way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like a reversal signal but is simply part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Septuagesima is the third Sunday before Lent in the Christian calendar, a feast day of the church.

clue.text: Ineffectual American drug? Not so

parts.note: E is slang for ecstasy
less means not so much, to a smaller degree

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a US drug is any good and is told no.
explanation.definitionFit: Useless means having no effect or value, which is ineffectual.

clue.text: Like a style of painting some revel in early

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some people enjoy a particular art style when they are young.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear painting stresses outline and drawn line rather than colour and tone, as in Wölfflin's art-historical term.

clue.text: Tedious book lying around Irish quarters

indicators.note: the book lies around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: a tome is a large book
E and S are compass points, quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A dull book has been left lying in an Irish lodging.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiresome means wearying or boring, the same as tedious.

clue.text: Benefactors having no right to infiltrate parties

indicators.note: these letters get inside the parties, slipping in among them

parts.note: dos are parties or celebrations
taken as written

explanation.surface: Charitable givers are refusing to let right-wingers gatecrash their parties.
explanation.definitionFit: Donors are people who give money or goods, as benefactors do.

clue.text: Capital Henry invested in high-quality food shop

indicators.note: money invested in something goes inside it

parts.note: a deli, short for delicatessen, sells fine foods
H is the symbol for the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry puts his money into an upmarket deli.
explanation.definitionFit: Delhi, as New Delhi, is the capital city of India.

clue.text: Newspaper's revolutionary work plugged by Times leader

indicators.note: a plug fills a hole, so the first letters have the leader stopped inside them

parts.note: red means communist, revolutionary
OP, short for opus, is a work

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of Times

explanation.surface: A paper's radical article is promoted by the editor of The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugged' tempts as 'advertised'; here it means filled, like a hole.
explanation.definitionFit: A red-top is a British tabloid newspaper, so called for its red masthead.

clue.text: Acclaim register, one used endlessly by Brussels

indicators.note: placed beside: the Brussels letters sit next to the rest, at the front

parts.note: Brussels is the seat of the EU, which it stands for
a log is a register or record
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: without either end, so the first and last letters of the following word are lost

explanation.surface: A record book has been worn down by EU bureaucrats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' strips both ends of 'used', leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise is to praise highly, especially in a speech, which is to acclaim.

clue.text: Set cricket side up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field

explanation.surface: A cricket team has been put in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To gel is to set, as a jelly does when it solidifies.

clue.text: Cook disturbed by a brawl

indicators.note: the cooking word is interrupted, with the letter breaking into it

parts.note: to fry is to cook

explanation.surface: A cook's work is interrupted by a punch-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A fray is a noisy fight or quarrel, a synonym of brawl.

clue.text: Improving technique increases murder rate

parts.note: ups as a verb means increases
killing is murder; read with 'increases', the phrase says the murder rate goes up

explanation.surface: Better technique makes a gangland death toll rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'ups killing', the answer literally says the murder rate increases.
explanation.definitionFit: Upskilling is training to improve one's skills, so it is a matter of improving technique.
